title: Hybrid conversation bands — back-of-envelope
content:
Quick scratchpad: hybrid conversation bands idea (session bundles + per-message micro-billing). Purpose: give a few concrete unit-econ worked examples to share with GTM and see which combos are sane for small startups vs. enterprise pilots.

Assumptions (baseline):
- baseline model cost to Redwood (amortized infra + tokens + ops) = $0.004 per 1k output tokens (conservative midline).
- median request: 80 input tokens + 120 output tokens ~ 200 tokens per turn.
- average messages per session (end-user chat) = 6 turns (could be 3 for search assistants, 12+ for long workflows).
- tokens per session ≈ 200 tokens/turn * 6 turns = 1,200 tokens/session.
- other infra overhead / routing / KV cache costs add ~20% on top of token cost for smallish sessions.
- target gross margin = 65% for hosted API at scale (we can accept lower for PLG entry offers).

Derived cost numbers: 
- raw token cost per session = 1,200 tokens * ($0.004/1k) = 1.2 * $0.004 = $0.0048 ~ $0.005
- add 20% overhead => full cost/session ≈ $0.006
- to hit 65% gross margin, price/session = cost / (1 - 0.65) = $0.006 / 0.35 ≈ $0.017 => ~1.7 cents/session.

This looks very low — because model cost assumption is low. For larger models or longer context maybe 10x. Let's run a conservative scenario x10: 
- cost/session = $0.06 => price to customer @65% margin = $0.06 / 0.35 = $0.171 => ~17 cents/session.

Pricing format ideas:
A) Session-bands (simple PLG)
- Free tier: 50 sessions/month; Starter: $15/mo -> 1,000 sessions included (~1.5¢/session effective) ; Overage 2.5¢/session.
- Pro: $150/mo -> 12,000 sessions included (~1.25¢/session) ; enterprise: custom.
Rationale: aligns well with consumer chat apps and low-touch onboarding. Overage protects against heavy tails.

B) Seat + token-bucket (mixed)
- Seat $60/mo includes 5,000 tokens/day (150k tokens/mo). Extra tokens charged at $0.003/1k.
- Example: product analytics tool with 2k sessions/mo (assume 1.2k tokens/session => 2.4M tokens) => included 150k tokens + 2.25M extra => 2.25M/1k * $0.003 = $6.75 => Effective monthly cost = $60 + $6.75 = $66.75 => ~3.3¢/session.
Rationale: predictable seat fee for teams; token bucket smooths variability and caps runaway costs.

C) Hybrid bands + burst credits (target: enterprise pilots)
- Band A (light): up to 5k sessions/mo @ $0.02/session; Band B (med): next 50k sessions @ $0.012/session; Band C (bulk): >55k sessions negotiated, e.g., $0.007/session.
- Burst credits: prebuy 1M tokens for $30 (discounted) to use for spikes (applied per model family).

Worked examples (conservative model cost x10 case):
1) Early startup: 10k sessions/mo (1.2k tokens/session => 12M tokens)
- If session-bands starter: price = $0.02/session => $200/mo -> cost to Redwood = 12M tokens * ($0.004/1k * 10x?) wait careful. Use conservative per-1k token cost = $0.04 (x10).
- infra cost = 12,000 * 1.2k tokens = 14.4M tokens => charge basis: tokens/1k * $0.04 = 14,400 * $0.04 = $576 cost.
- Revenue = 10k * $0.02 = $200 (loss). So session pricing must be priced higher vs. heavy token usages.

Lesson: session pricing works only if average tokens/session are lower or we price higher. For token-heavy apps, bucket or per-token is better.

Sensitivity table (quick mental):
- If tokens/session = 600 (short conversational flows), cost/session (conservative) = 0.6k * $0.04 = $0.024 -> price@65% margin =~ $0.069 (6.9¢).
- If tokens/session = 1.2k -> cost/session = $0.048 -> price@65% =~ $0.137 (13.7¢).
- If tokens/session = 2.4k -> cost/session = $0.096 -> price@65% =~ $0.274 (27.4¢).

Open questions / tradeoffs (write-up notes):
- Do we want simple session-bands for PLG even if noisy? It helps adoption but can be loss-leading for long contexts.
- Can we auto-detect model size / expected token usage per route and charge per-token for heavy routes while keeping session-pricing for UI flows? (Implementation complexity + clarity risk).
- How to present to customers: "Sessions" is simple for product teams, but opaque for finance. Need an explainer showing average tokens per session and a calculator.
- Burst credits: how to price so enterprises love precommit but we don't cannibalize monthly revenue? Offer ~15–30% discount vs paygo.

Quick TODOs:
- build a 1-pager with 3 starter bundles (low / mid / high) + sample customer fit and callouts (privacy, private deployments).
- compute accurate backend cost numbers per model family (Llama2-70B, FP16 quantized, etc.) — talk to infra/applied-ml to get 1k-token cost ranges. (Ethan: ping for numbers).
- prototype a small calculator spreadsheet: inputs = tokens/turn, turns/session, sessions/mo, model family -> outputs = cost, price@target-margin, suggested band.

Notes to self: keep PLG tier names simple (Starter / Scale / Enterprise). Avoid too many micro-pricing knobs early. But surface advanced toggles in console (per-route overrides, default model family).

Slack threads and references: #pricing-playbooks, PRIC-321, convo-bands-proposal on Confluence (linked above).

End of scratchpad — will refine after infra cost numbers available.

Fragments and questions for future edits: 
- Could we include "session length meter" in console so customers see tokens/session histogram? That would reduce disputes.
- Maybe a hybrid "session credit" currency: 1 credit = 500 tokens; sell credits in packs. Simpler mental model for non-technical buyers.
- Should overage be per-session or per-token? Per-token is fairer but harder to explain.
